phase.title: Persistence, resume, and execution lifecycle
phase.goal: Make sessions and runs durable, resumable under documented rules, cancellable, and fully traceable.

why_this_phase_exists: Add durable lifecycle guarantees around the already working Harness without coupling the Agent Loop to a database or replaying uncertain external side effects.
in_scope: Define one minimal ExecutionStore boundary for the persistence operations the Harness actually needs; do not create one repository interface per entity by default.
Implement a durable local persistence adapter suitable for the assessment demo.
Persist session and run state before acknowledging lifecycle changes.
Persist every model step, tool request, tool result, error, cancellation request, and terminal transition.
Implement session reload and continuation with prior messages available to the agent.
Define startup recovery behavior for runs left in a non-terminal state.
Implement cooperative cancellation, including behavior for an in-flight model or tool call.
Prevent concurrent active runs from corrupting a session through an explicit concurrency policy.
Keep current Run snapshots, ordered events, transcript messages, and tool execution records distinct without adopting full event sourcing.
Define how diagnostically recorded late results are prevented from changing a cancelled Run or scheduling more work.
out_of_scope: A repository interface for every stored entity
Automatic replay of interrupted Runs or ambiguous side-effecting tool calls
boundaries_introduced: ExecutionStore is implemented by persistence infrastructure and consumed by the Harness; AgentLoop has no database dependency.
Run snapshots serve status reads, ordered events serve audit and streaming, and messages and tool records preserve execution context and trace details.
Persistence technology and schema can change without changing the Agent Loop.
contracts_introduced: Persisted Session, Run, Message, ToolCall, ToolResult, RuntimeError, and Event records use the typed JSON-serializable core shapes from Phase 1.
Event retrieval uses monotonically increasing per-Run sequence values rather than timestamps as ordering cursors.
When supported by the chosen store, a lifecycle state transition and its corresponding event are committed consistently in one transaction.
At most one active Run is allowed per Session for this assessment implementation.

lifecycle_policy.session_resume: A new run may continue an existing session using the persisted conversation and prior terminal run history.
lifecycle_policy.interrupted_run: On startup, a run found in a non-terminal execution state is marked interrupted; it is not automatically replayed because a prior tool may have produced an external side effect.
lifecycle_policy.cancellation: Record the cancellation request immediately, signal the active operation when supported, discard late results from scheduling further work, and persist a cancelled terminal event.
lifecycle_policy.queued_cancellation: A queued Run may transition directly to cancelled without starting model or tool work.
lifecycle_policy.late_results: A late provider or tool result may be stored as diagnostic information, but it is never fed to the model, never schedules another step, and never changes cancelled to completed.
lifecycle_policy.concurrency: Allow at most one active run per session unless a stronger isolation design is implemented and documented.
lifecycle_policy.event_ordering: Persist a unique event ID and monotonically increasing per-run sequence number in the same transaction as the corresponding state change where supported.
lifecycle_policy.delivery_guarantee: Claim only durable recording and deterministic ordering provided by the chosen local store; do not claim exactly-once external tool execution.

deliverables: Minimal ExecutionStore boundary kept outside Agent Loop logic
Durable local persistence adapter and schema migrations

acceptance_criteria.criterion: A process restart preserves sessions, messages, runs, events, tool calls, and terminal outputs.
A new run can resume a prior session and the model receives the documented conversation context.
Cancelling an active run prevents any subsequent model or tool step from being scheduled and ends in a persisted cancelled state.
A run interrupted by process termination is identified on restart and handled according to the documented non-replay policy.
A complete ordered audit trace can be retrieved for a run, including failed tool attempts.
Cancelling the same queued, running, or already terminal Run repeatedly is safe and does not create invalid lifecycle transitions.
A late external result after cancellation cannot be fed to the model, schedule new work, or convert the Run to completed.

required_tests: Resume a session in a new run
Persist tool failure and retry attempts
Cancel during a slow tool call
Idempotent cancellation of queued, running, and terminal Runs
Ignore a late result after cancellation
Recover a run left active by simulated process interruption
Reject or serialize concurrent runs for the same session
Verify event sequence ordering after restart
Verify a state transition and its event remain consistent under a simulated storage failure
deferred_decisions: Concrete RPC transport and public response envelope
Distributed locking and horizontal worker coordination
Exactly-once external execution, which is intentionally not claimed
Production retention, archival, and multi-tenant storage policy
exit_condition: Sessions and traces survive restart, resume behavior is explicit, and cancellation or interruption cannot silently schedule additional work.
